findings.reason: every recorded head in the mounted ledgers is 40 characters (1831 rows read, none abbreviated), so with dispatched heads of 12 or 40 the two rules coincide on the whole observed population and the divergence needs a record shape that does not occur; it is worth knowing before §4 publishes per-row commands, not worth an edit that reopens the plan-wide gate.
findings.text: §3 calls its same-as-recorded refusal "the complement of §2's rule that a row is mismatched when its recorded head does not begin with its dispatched head", but the shipped census classifies a row mismatched on `not recorded.lower().startswith(dispatched.lower())` (`scripts/review_rows_with_another_rounds_verdict.py:198`) while the verb refuses on `same_revision`, which is true when *either* head is a prefix of the other — so a row whose recorded head were the shorter abbreviation of a longer dispatched head (a `.at-<full-40>` write path with a 12-character `reviewed_head_sha`) would be listed by §2 as mismatched and refused by §3, and §4 publishes a `supersede-review` command for every listed row.
